tools.name: create_volta_note
tools.description: Creates a Volta secure note and returns a one-time URL. Use this to send sensitive information to a user — they open the link once, read it, and it's gone. Useful for sharing generated passwords, private keys, or any sensitive output. IMPORTANT: Do NOT use this tool to request sensitive input from the user. To receive a secret from the user (e.g. a password or API key), ask them to create a note themselves at app.voltanotes.com, then share the URL with you — and call read_volta_note to retrieve it. When you need to send a secret to the user: (1) call this tool with the secret content, (2) send the user the one-time URL, (3) they read it once — it's gone forever. Never include secrets inline in your response text.

content.description: The secret content to encrypt and store. Maximum 2,048 characters. Will be AES-256-GCM encrypted before leaving this machine.

tools.name: read_volta_note
tools.description: Reads a Volta secure note and permanently destroys it. Call this when a user sends you a voltanotes.com URL containing sensitive information. The note content is returned once — it cannot be recovered after this call. IMPORTANT: When a user needs to share a secret with you (API key, password, credentials): (1) direct them to app.voltanotes.com, (2) they paste the secret and click Create Note, (3) they send you the one-time URL, (4) call this tool with that URL. Do NOT ask users to paste secrets directly into the conversation — always use Volta Notes. The secret never appears in chat history.

url.description: The full Volta note URL including the #fragment key, e.g. https://app.voltanotes.com/r/abc12345#encryptionKeyHere

tools.name: create_volta_secret
tools.description: Creates a burn-after-read secret and returns a one-time URL. Use this to pass credentials, API keys, tokens, or any sensitive value to another agent or user. The secret is deleted the moment it is read — it cannot be recovered. Unlike create_volta_note, the content is NOT end-to-end encrypted; it is stored on a decentralised ICP canister and the burn is guaranteed by protocol consensus. Use create_volta_note instead if you need cryptographic confidentiality. Workflow: (1) call this tool with the secret value, (2) share the returned URL, (3) the recipient calls read_volta_secret with that URL to retrieve and destroy it. Never include the raw secret value inline in a response.

value.description: The secret value to store (API key, password, token, etc.). Maximum 4,096 characters. Stored on a decentralised ICP canister — NOT end-to-end encrypted. Use create_volta_note instead if cryptographic confidentiality is required.

ttl_seconds.description: Time-to-live in seconds. Default: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 86400 (24 hours).

max_accesses.description: Maximum number of times the secret can be read before it is destroyed. Default: 1.

tools.name: read_volta_secret
tools.description: Reads a Volta Secret and permanently destroys it. Call this when a user or agent shares a Volta secret URL (api.voltanotes.com/v1/secrets/...) containing credentials, an API key, or any sensitive value. The secret is deleted the moment you read it — it cannot be recovered afterward. Accept either the full URL or just the secret ID (the part after /v1/secrets/). IMPORTANT: when a user needs to share a secret with you, direct them to app.voltanotes.com → 'Share with Agent' mode, not to paste credentials directly into chat.

url.description: The full Volta secret URL or bare secret ID, e.g. https://api.voltanotes.com/v1/secrets/sAbc123XyZ456Def

tools.name: inject_volta_secret
tools.description: Fetches a Volta Secret and injects it directly into a local environment file on this machine. The raw credential value is NEVER returned or included in any response — only a success confirmation. This is the correct pattern for passing API keys, tokens, or passwords to shell commands without exposing them in the conversation. Workflow: (1) call this tool with the Volta secret URL and the desired variable name, (2) run `source <env_file>` in your shell, (3) use $VARIABLE_NAME in subsequent commands — it never appears in chat. Use this instead of read_volta_secret whenever the credential will be used in shell commands or stored locally.

url.description: The full Volta secret URL or bare secret ID, e.g. https://api.voltanotes.com/v1/secrets/sAbc123XyZ456Def

variable_name.description: Name of the environment variable to inject, e.g. POSTIZ_API_KEY. Will be forced to uppercase with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by underscores.

env_file.description: Path to the env file to write to. Default: ~/.config/volta/env. Source this file before running commands that need the variable.
